basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'Vers. 12. Et alebat eos, etc. Solent quaerere hoc loco unde jumenta et pecora viverent,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 12. Et alebat eos, etc. Solent quaerere hoc loco unde jumenta et pecora viverent, fame per septem annos omnem terram premente, maxime quia filii Jacob dixerunt superius non esse sibi pabula in terra Chanaan, eo quod nullae ibi essent pluviae. Sed sciendum Nilum in Aegypto maximas facere paludes, in quibus abundans herba nascitur jumentis et pabula pecoribus tanto fertiliora quanto siccior fuerit Nilus. In his ergo locis alebantur jumenta et caetera animalia, quae plurima erant in Aegypto.
